claims.statement: Water-loss guidance is an internal operational aid rather than coverage authority: coverage decisions must use the policy and attached endorsement in force, and investigation, inspection, mitigation authorization, or payment does not by itself waive policy rights or accept the full claim (H.0.1-H.0.2, H.0.11, H.6.7, H.7.3, H.7.6-H.7.8).

The water-loss intake workflow opens a distinct claim file, records source, affected locations, discovery date, and reporter, confirms policy and identity details, acknowledges receipt, communicates investigation status, instructs mitigation within three days after discovery, and issues a reservation of rights within ten days after identifying facts that may limit or preclude coverage when a final decision is not yet supportable (H.6.1-H.6.10).

Notice timing is contract-specific rather than a universal 30-day rule: HO 04 90 requires notice within 30 days after discovery, HO 04 27 and DP 04 95 require notice within 30 days after loss, while the HO-3 2024-03 base form requires prompt notice with the insured, location, and available circumstances.

A water-loss investigation must independently establish source, water path, duration or recurrence, and the connection between the event and direct physical damage; prior loss alone does not establish that current damage is excluded, and conflicting or incomplete causation evidence must be documented and referred when material (H.5.1-H.5.8, H.5.17, H.5.37-H.5.40, H.6.12-H.6.19).

The HO-3 2024-03 base form covers direct physical loss from accidental discharge or overflow of listed plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, sprinkler, or household-appliance systems, but excludes continuous or repeated seepage and does not cover loss to the system or appliance from which water escaped; its water-backup and sump exclusions remain unless an applicable endorsement changes them (P.9, P.29-P.33, X.8-X.9).

HO 04 90 W.1 writes back HO-3 P.9 and X.8-X.9 for water backup and sump discharge or overflow, including sudden or gradual covered water events, while preserving flood, surface-water, maintenance, failed-equipment, and other stated exclusions; HO 04 27 instead covers specified accidental water damage but excludes sewer, drain, and sump backup; DP 04 95 supplies its own water-backup and sump-overflow grant and conditions.

For covered water-backup losses, HO 04 90 (2027-01) applies a single $10,000 limit across covered loss and expenses arising from the same water event and a $1,000 deductible applied to covered damage from the same occurrence; DP 04 95 (2021-05) applies a $5,000 aggregate water-backup limit and a $1,000 deductible applied once to the same covered loss.

HO 04 27 (2016-05) applies a $2,500 limit to sewer or drain backup and sump overflow and a $5,000 limit to fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria; those limits apply regardless of claimants, locations, items, or causes and are not combined, with the applicable policy deductible applied to the covered loss.

The claim scope must separate covered direct physical damage, reasonable emergency mitigation, source-component work, pre-existing or maintenance conditions, improvements, contents, and other-insurance or salvage effects; valuation and payment are limited to supported covered loss under the applicable form, with HO-3 dwelling replacement-cost treatment dependent on the 80-percent threshold and HO 04 90 and DP 04 95 using their stated evidence-based settlement provisions (H.6.11, H.6.21-H.6.25, H.6.31, H.7.25-H.7.29).

Water-loss claims must be escalated when claimed, incurred, or reasonably anticipated exposure exceeds $25,000, without waiting for final value, and also when source, duration, exclusion, limitation, endorsement, competing scope, shared responsibility, suspected fraud, contamination, representation, litigation, or unusual compromise issues require authority review (H.5.9-H.5.17, H.5.21-H.5.36, H.7.4-H.7.5, H.7.17-H.7.18, H.7.20-H.7.48).

Payment handling requires authority and payee checks, application of the form-specific limit and deductible, separate expense and indemnity authority, and prompt payment of supported undisputed amounts; denials or partial denials require a written explanation tied accurately to the applicable policy language (H.6.38-H.6.45, H.7.9-H.7.11). Under HO-3 2024-03, covered loss is payable within 60 days after agreement, final judgment, or filing of an appraisal award, while appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage or policy interpretation (S.35, S.42-S.47).

Closure requires a documented coverage decision, payment status, unresolved issues, required communications, evidence and recovery handling, and preservation of claim notes and payment records; a claim must be reopened when credible new information may affect coverage, damages, payment, or recovery rights (H.6.43-H.6.54).

The current HO-3 and DP-3 begin with an ordinance-or-law exclusion for enforcement and compliance costs, while HO 04 16 modifies that insurance and controls over conflicting policy language for ordinance-or-law coverage.

The supplied base forms have materially different built-in ordinance-or-law arrangements: DP-3 provides 20% of Coverage A within Coverage A, HO-3 provides 15% of Coverage A as additional insurance, HO-4 has no Coverage A despite a Coverage-A reference in its Additional Coverages, HO-5 provides 15% within Coverage A, and HO-6 provides 15% without reducing Coverage A.

Both HO 04 16 editions require covered direct physical loss caused by an insured peril, an in-force and legally applicable ordinance or law enforced by the responsible governmental authority, and a required cost attributable to that covered loss; code-only loss, voluntary compliance, unrelated prior conditions, and elective betterment do not satisfy the trigger.

After the trigger is satisfied, HO 04 16 addresses loss in value of a required-to-be-demolished undamaged portion, required demolition and resulting debris removal, and the incremental cost to repair, rebuild, or replace covered property for compliance; the 2018 edition expressly enumerates required building, safety, utility, accessibility, permit, inspection, and design-related work, while the 2023 edition limits professional services to those necessary for covered compliance work.

HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 provides a 10% of Coverage A ordinance-or-law limit in addition to Coverage A and permits payment as work progresses or after completion while allowing payment to be withheld until covered construction is completed and supported.

HO 04 16 edition 2023-11 raises the ordinance-or-law limit to 25% of Coverage A as additional insurance and applies one aggregate limit across affected Coverage A property, requirements, authorities, claims, repair or rebuilding, demolition, and related debris; increased construction cost is tied to repair or replacement at the same residence premises unless prohibited and to reasonable actually incurred expenses.

Both HO 04 16 editions apply a deductible to covered ordinance-or-law loss and require evidence of the governmental requirement, cost, and work; the editions require notice, preservation of records, inspection access, and supporting plans, permits, invoices, and proof of incurred or completed work.

The 2023 HO 04 16 limit is tied to property insured under Coverage A and a covered building, so the endorsement's Coverage-A percentage cannot be assumed to transfer to a form that does not provide Coverage A, such as the supplied HO-4.

Roof settlement and ordinance-or-law coverage are separate: the roof must first have covered direct physical loss, the base HO-3 and DP-3 default to replacement-cost settlement for roof surfacing unless a roof schedule endorsement applies, and HO 23 74 instead settles roof surfacing at actual cash value at age twelve or more without itself creating or removing code coverage.

The supplied materials are Mississippi form editions, and the DP-3 makes an applicable-law-required provision control over a conflicting policy term; the water-loss handling guide is operational and noncontractual and therefore is not authority for deciding whether code-related costs are insured.

The DP-3 editions form a supersession chain: 2012-11 is superseded by 2020-08 for policies effective on or after 2020-08-01, and 2020-08 is superseded by 2026-01 for policies effective on or after 2026-01-01; each superseded edition remains applicable to policies written under it.
DP-3 building coverage uses an open-peril structure for Coverage A and Coverage B, while Coverage C personal property requires a peril expressly described in the applicable edition's perils section.

Coverage A replacement-cost settlement changes by edition: 2012-11 requires insurance of at least 80% of pre-loss replacement cost, 2020-08 requires 90% of full replacement cost, and 2026-01 returns to 80% while also requiring reasonably prompt repair or replacement and applying ACV when the replacement-cost conditions are not met.
Coverage B is limited to 10% of Coverage A in 2012-11 and 2020-08, and increases to 15% of Coverage A in 2026-01; the 2026 form also expressly limits payment to the insured's financial interest.

Coverage C has a stated limit of 0% of Coverage A in all three supplied DP-3 editions, but its location and property grants expand in later editions to include temporarily removed, newly acquired-residence, transported, and other-location property subject to the applicable form.

Coverage D is limited to 20% of Coverage A in 2012-11, 25% in 2020-08, and 30% in 2026-01; the 2020 form adds a civil-authority access provision, while the 2026 form ties payment to actual lost rent and ends it when the rented part is usable or the rental activity is permanently relocated.

Across the editions, DP-3 excludes flood and surface water, below-ground water, sewer or drain backup absent applicable coverage, earth movement, ordinance-or-law costs unless provided, gradual seepage or leakage, faulty work, deterioration, and other listed causes, while allowing resulting or ensuing direct physical loss only where the applicable edition says the resulting loss is separately covered.

Coverage C in 2026-01 is a named-peril grant that expressly lists fire or lightning, windstorm or hail, explosion, riot or civil commotion, aircraft, vehicles, smoke, vandalism or malicious mischief, theft, volcanic eruption, falling objects, weight of ice snow or sleet, sudden system discharge, freezing, and artificially generated electrical current, followed by specific exclusions.

Coverage E changes materially by edition: 2012-11 provides a 5% additional debris-removal amount, 5% vegetation aggregate with a $500 per-item cap, and a $500 fire-department service charge; 2020-08 uses 10%, a 10% vegetation aggregate with a $750 per-item cap, and $750; 2026-01 uses 15%, a 10% vegetation aggregate with a $1,000 per-item cap, and $1,000, and expressly details removed property, credit-card or access-device loss, grave markers, and collapse.

The editions impose different claim-settlement mechanics: the minimum Section I deductible is $500 in 2012-11, $1,000 in 2020-08, and $1,500 in 2026-01; proof of loss is due within 60 days after request in 2012-11 and 90 days after request in 2020-08 and 2026-01; payment follows the stated 60-day, 45-day, and 30-day rules respectively; appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage.

DP 04 95 Water Backup is an optional DP endorsement that controls conflicting base-form language when attached, covers direct physical loss from sewer or drain backup and sump overflow, retains exclusions for flood and other causes, has a $5,000 aggregate limit, and applies a $1,000 deductible once per covered water-backup loss.

The Florida DP 01 09 overlay controls conflicts, imposes a 2% to 10% windstorm-and-hail deductible, requires 45 days' notice for an increase, defines a Named Storm Period through 72 hours after designation ends, and supplies Florida cancellation and claim-handling deadlines including 14-day acknowledgment, 90-business-day decision after requested items, and 20-business-day payment after acceptance.

The Texas DP 01 45 overlay applies to Texas property and Texas-law losses, controls conflicts, imposes a 1% to 5% windstorm-or-hail deductible, requires 30 days' notice for a deductible increase, defines a 72-hour post-designation Named Storm Period, and supplies Texas cancellation and claim-handling deadlines including 15-day acknowledgment, 15-business-day decision after requested items, and five-business-day payment after acceptance.

The Texas overlay changes the 2026-01 DP-3 roof settlement rule by requiring actual-cash-value valuation for covered roof damage when the roof is at least ten years old unless another policy provision is broader, whereas DP-3 2026-01 otherwise states replacement cost for roof surfacing unless an ACV roof-schedule endorsement is attached.

DP-3 claim conditions require notice, mitigation, preservation and inspection of damaged property, records and inventories, cooperation, proof of loss, and preservation of recovery rights; later editions expressly permit denial only to the extent a required-duty failure materially affects the loss or claim, so later material-prejudice wording must not be back-applied to earlier editions.

HO-3 edition selection is governed by policy effective date: 2011-05 applies to policies effective before 2018-09-01 under that edition, 2018-09 applies from 2018-09-01 until superseded for policies effective on or after 2024-03-01, and 2024-03 applies from 2024-03-01; superseded editions remain governing for policies written under them.

The 2024 filing memorandum explains the stated rationale for HO-3 2024-03 changes, but the form’s agreement and authorized-written-action provisions make the filed form controlling when the memorandum and contract text differ; an attached endorsement controls over inconsistent base-form language only within its stated scope.

Across editions, HO-3 Section I contains Coverages A through D, Additional Coverages, perils, exclusions, and conditions, while Section II contains personal liability and medical payments coverage; the recurring organization does not make the edition-specific grants and exclusions interchangeable.

Coverage B remains 10% of Coverage A and Coverage C remains 50% of Coverage A across the three editions, while later editions expressly characterize Coverage B as additional insurance and keep Coverage C special limits within the Coverage C limit.

Coverage A evolves from the 2011 direct-physical-loss and 80%-replacement-cost framework, through the 2018 fixture and dwelling-service-property wording, to the 2024 Declarations-based residence-premises grant with a separate roof-surfacing settlement provision; the 2024 memorandum identifies these as dwelling, direct-loss, and roof-payment-floor clarifications.

Coverage C special limits are edition-specific: 2024 changes the 2018 amounts for cash, jewelry theft, firearms theft, and silverware theft, leaves watercraft, business-property, and electronic-apparatus amounts at their 2018 levels, and the 2011 form states lower amounts for most of those categories.

Coverage D remains 20% of Coverage A, but 2011, 2018, and 2024 use different operative descriptions: 2018 expressly uses actual-loss-sustained and civil-authority access concepts, while 2024 details temporary lodging, meals, relocation, storage, and direct causation; the memorandum says the revision ties loss of use to the applicable covered loss.

Additional Coverages materially change across editions: 2011 provides 5% debris removal, 5% vegetation with a $500 per-item limit, and a $500 fire-department cap; 2018 keeps debris at 5% and raises the latter caps to $750; 2024 raises debris to 10%, vegetation to 10% of Coverage A with a $1,000 per-item cap, and the fire-department cap to $1,000, and adds stated card, assessment, ordinance-or-law, and grave-marker amounts.

The edition-specific water provisions differ: 2011 excludes backup, repeated seepage, subsurface water, and flood including water driven by wind or another force; 2018 expressly covers sudden and accidental system discharge or overflow while excluding repeated seepage and backup; and 2024 separately states accidental discharge, sudden-and-accidental system damage, off-premises plumbing discharge, and flood/surface-water exclusions using the phrase whether water is driven by wind or another force.

The 2024 Section I exclusion lead-in excludes loss caused directly or indirectly by an excluded peril, including concurrent or sequential contribution unless the policy expressly provides otherwise; the memorandum explains the concurrent-cause revision but does not replace that operative text.

The 2024 base form adds a roof-surfacing settlement floor and excludes cosmetic wind or hail damage that does not impair water shedding, while HO 23 74 is a separate attached endorsement whose 2018-09 edition used a 15-year actual-cash-value threshold and whose later 2025-05 edition uses a 12-year threshold.

Water-backup and wind or hail percentage-deductible protection are endorsement-dependent rather than automatic base-form coverage: the base forms exclude or limit those causes, while HO 04 90 and HO 23 77 provide edition-specific attached coverage or deductible terms and control only within their stated scope.

The 2024 post-loss conditions require notice, mitigation, preservation and inspection, records and inventory when requested, recovery-right preservation, and a signed sworn proof of loss within 90 days after request; the 2018 form required the sworn proof within 60 days, and the memorandum identifies the 90-day revision.

The 2024 form sets a $500 Section I deductible minimum, provides payment within 60 days after agreement, binding appraisal, or final judgment, and states that appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage, policy interpretation, or compliance.

Section II changes by edition: 2011 provides a compact Coverage E liability grant and three-year Coverage F medical-expense period; 2018 reorganizes Coverage E around defined occurrence, suit, and coverage territory terms and expressly states fault-free Coverage F; 2024 adds on-behalf-of liability wording, personal-activities and separate-insured scope, defense expenses and bond premiums, while retaining no-fault Coverage F and the three-year period.

The 2024 Section II exclusion lead-in expressly includes personal injury and denies a duty to defend claims or suits seeking damages excluded by Section II, whereas the 2011 lead-in addresses bodily injury and property damage without that personal-injury and excluded-defense wording; 2018 sits between them with an expanded exclusion structure.

The 2024 repository form contains apparent duplicated or malformed phrases in DEF.12, Coverage A.22, and certain cross-references; those textual defects should be flagged or quoted rather than silently corrected, because the filing memorandum cannot rewrite the controlling form.

The HO-4 2013-07 edition is superseded by HO-4 2021-10 for policies effective on or after 2021-10-01, while 2013-07 remains applicable to policies written under that edition; the two forms have effective dates 2013-07-01 and 2021-10-01 respectively.

Both HO-4 editions expressly provide no Coverage A, so the policy does not insure the dwelling or building property under Coverage A; Coverage D and some additional-coverages provisions nevertheless reference a Coverage A limit and must not be converted into assumed dwelling coverage.

HO-4 organizes property protection through Coverage B Other Structures, Coverage C Personal Property, and Coverage D Loss of Use, while Section I Coverage E contains Additional Coverages and Section II Coverage E and Coverage F provide Personal Liability and Medical Payments to Others.

The Coverage B settlement wording changed between editions: 2013-07 uses actual cash value when repair or replacement is not completed and permits repair, rebuilding, or replacement, while 2021-10 limits payment to the lesser of repair or replacement cost, actual cash value, or the Coverage B limit and permits taking paid-for property at the value paid.

The 2021-10 Coverage C special limits increased from 2013-07 for electronic apparatus in a motor vehicle, money and precious metals, theft of jewelry/watches/precious stones, theft of firearms, watercraft, and business property on the residence premises; the silverware limit remained $2,500 in both editions.

Coverage D covers qualifying additional living expense, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss of use, subject to records, mitigation, and covered-loss conditions; its stated limit changed from 30% of the Coverage A limit in 2013-07 to 40% in 2021-10.

The HO-4 base forms exclude major water boundaries including flood/surface water, subsurface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow or discharge, and continuous or repeated seepage or leakage, along with deterioration and fungi/rot/bacteria conditions; covered sudden and accidental discharge is subject to the edition's peril wording and exclusions.

The editions require material post-loss duties including prompt notice, protection and retention of damaged property, inventories and records, examination under oath, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, cooperation, recovery-right preservation, and appraisal limited to amount-of-loss issues; the forms state a 60-day payment rule after agreement or other specified resolution.

Section II Coverage E pays covered occurrence-based bodily-injury or property-damage liability and provides a defense for a covered suit until the applicable liability limit is exhausted; Coverage F pays qualifying medical expenses to persons other than insureds without regard to fault, generally for expenses incurred within three years of the accident, subject to edition-specific exclusions.

HO 04 92 Water Backup — Tenants (2019-03) writes back limited direct-physical-loss coverage for covered personal property caused by defined water backup, subject to a $2,500 limit and $250 deductible, while preserving other policy exclusions and not creating coverage for otherwise ineligible property.

HO 04 27 Limited Water Damage Coverage (2016-05) modifies HO-4 water-damage terms by covering specified sudden and accidental discharge, overflow, breakage, or freezing events and preserves exclusions for repeated seepage, sewer/drain/sump backup, subsurface water, flood, fungi/rot/bacteria, and failed diversion systems; its stated limits include $2,500 for backup/sump overflow and $5,000 for fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria.

The seeded HO 04 61 Scheduled Personal Property editions and HO 04 65 Coverage C Increased Special Limits edition identify their line as HO-3 rather than HO-4, so they should not be applied as HO-4 endorsements without an applicable attachment or schedule establishing that use.

HO-5 2015-01 is superseded by HO-5 2022-06 for policies effective on or after 2022-06-01, but remains applicable to policies written under the older edition; the later edition is not retroactive merely because it exists in the form library.

Both HO-5 editions provide a broad risk-of-direct-physical-loss property grant rather than a short named-peril list, but payment still requires physical alteration or damage and remains subject to limits, deductibles, exclusions, location rules, special limits, and post-loss conditions; Coverage C mysterious disappearance is excluded unless evidence establishes theft or another covered cause.

The standard HO-5 property limits are 10% of Coverage A for Coverage B, 50% of Coverage A for Coverage C, and 20% of Coverage A for Coverage D in both 2015-01 and 2022-06. Coverage A uses replacement-cost settlement when insurance is at least 80% of full replacement cost and otherwise settles at actual cash value, subject to the edition's terms; 2022-06 additionally states replacement-cost treatment for roof surfacing unless an ACV roof-schedule endorsement applies.

Coverage C special limits materially increase in 2022-06 for jewelry theft from $2,500 to $3,000, firearms theft from $3,000 to $3,500, watercraft from $1,000 to $2,000, business property on the residence premises from $2,500 to $5,000, and electronic apparatus in a motor vehicle from $1,000 to $2,000; the $300 money or precious-metals limit and $5,000 silverware theft limit remain stated, while the 2022-06 form retains the 50% aggregate Coverage C limit.

The principal additional-coverages amounts in the supplied 2015-01 and 2022-06 texts are aligned: debris removal can receive an additional 10% when the applicable limit is exhausted, vegetation is 5% of Coverage A with a $1,000 per-item limit, fire-department service charge is $1,000, card and forgery or counterfeit loss is $2,500, loss assessment is $2,500, ordinance-or-law coverage is 15% of Coverage A within Coverage A, landlord's furnishings are $2,500, grave markers are $7,500, and refrigerated property is $1,500. Additional limits do not create coverage for excluded property or causes.

Both editions exclude major property-loss boundaries including flood and surface water, underground water, sewer or sump backup, earth movement, ordinance-or-law costs, governmental action, war, nuclear hazard, pollutants, deterioration, mechanical breakdown, faulty work, mold or microbial conditions, repeated seepage, vacancy-related losses, construction theft, and unexplained disappearance; both preserve resulting direct physical loss only where the applicable wording independently covers it, and 2022-06 expressly addresses roof-surfacing and cosmetic roof treatment.

Coverage E in both editions pays damages for which an insured is legally liable because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for a covered suit until the applicable occurrence limit is exhausted; Coverage F pays necessary medical expenses without regard to fault when its conditions apply, requires expenses within three years after the accident, and uses a declarations limit per injured person. The 2022-06 Section II additional coverage reduces damage to property of others from $2,500 in 2015-01 to $1,000.

The HO-5 claim conditions require prompt notice, theft or criminal-loss reporting to law enforcement when applicable, reasonable mitigation and temporary repairs, preservation and inspection of damaged property, records and inventories, cooperation, and a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request in both editions. Either party may demand appraisal over amount of loss, each appraiser must be selected within 20 days, appraisal does not determine coverage or causation, and payment is due within 60 days after agreement; 2022-06 additionally expressly conditions a duty failure on material prejudice and permits payment delay while material information remains unavailable.

HO 05 24 Special Personal Property Coverage changes the policy only as stated, applies policy definitions and conditions otherwise, and controls over conflicting policy language; property ineligible under the policy remains ineligible unless the endorsement provides otherwise. If attached to an HO-5 assembly, it must therefore be read first as the acting document and then with the unchanged HO-5 provisions, but repository metadata identifies HO 05 24 as an HO-3 endorsement rather than an HO-5 form, so attachment and compatibility must be verified. Its stated jewelry-theft limit is $2,500 and it excludes mysterious disappearance among other listed losses.

HO 04 61 Scheduled Personal Property applies only to property specifically identified in the schedule and its stated limit, provides worldwide coverage for scheduled property including theft and qualifying disappearance, breakage, and accidental damage, and controls over conflicting policy language to the extent of the endorsement. The 2012-02 edition states a zero-dollar deductible for scheduled personal property, so that deductible cannot be carried forward to the 2020-11 edition without reading the later endorsement's own provisions.

HO 04 65 Coverage C — Increased Special Limits changes only the expressly increased Coverage C special limits; it does not create coverage, alter a peril, remove exclusions, change valuation, or eliminate a deductible. Its stated theft limits are $5,000 for jewelry, watches, and precious stones, $6,500 for firearms, and $10,000 for silverware, and repository metadata identifies it as an HO-3 endorsement whose attachment to an HO-5 must be confirmed.

The HO-6 2014-04 form is effective April 1, 2014 and is superseded by HO-6 2023-02 for policies effective on or after February 1, 2023, while remaining applicable to policies written under the earlier edition; HO-6 2023-02 is effective February 1, 2023.
HO 04 35 and HO 04 91 apply only when attached, and an attached endorsement controls over conflicting base-policy language within its stated scope.

HO-6 separates unit-owner property coverages A through D from Section I Additional Coverages and Section II liability coverages E and F; Section II Coverage E is Personal Liability and Section II Coverage F is Medical Payments to Others.

Under HO-6 2014-04, Coverage A covers unit building items and certain exclusively used or commonly owned property only to the extent of the insured's ownership interest or legal responsibility, has a default $5,000 limit, and uses an 80% Coverage A replacement-cost threshold with actual-cash-value treatment when the threshold or repair condition is not met.

Under HO-6 2023-02, Coverage A covers unit property, attached property, improvements, materials, and building property the insured is required to insure by agreement, has a default $10,000 limit, excludes land and listed exterior or association property absent contractual repair responsibility, and retains the 80% replacement-cost threshold with actual-cash-value treatment for unrepaired property.

Coverage B is separate from the unit building layer: 2014-04 covers the insured's interest in qualifying separate structures, including a jointly owned interest, while 2023-02 requires sole ownership and excludes an attached structure from Other Structures coverage.

Both HO-6 editions provide worldwide Coverage C personal-property treatment, but 2023-02 raises the stated special limits for money, jewelry, firearms, watercraft, business property, and electronic apparatus over the 2014-04 amounts while leaving the silverware limit at $2,500; these limits remain within Coverage C.

Both editions set Coverage D at 50% of the Coverage A limit and cover qualifying additional living expense, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss of use; 2023-02 expressly ends payment when the premises becomes fit or the insured permanently relocates and requires due diligence in repair or replacement.

HO-6 2014-04 lists named property perils and separately excludes flood, surface water, subsurface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow, earth movement, gradual seepage, defective conditions, pollutants, and intentional loss; HO-6 2023-02 retains the named-peril structure and adds detailed boundaries for water, vacancy, theft, collapse, roof surfacing, cosmetic damage, and utility failures.

Both HO-6 editions require prompt notice, protection and preservation of damaged property, inspection access, records, cooperation, and recovery-right preservation; both state a $500 minimum Section I deductible, require a sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, and provide payment within 60 days after agreement on the covered loss.

Section II Coverage E in both editions pays legally owed damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for a covered suit; 2023-02 states a more granular exclusion set than 2014-04, including business, rental, care-custody-control, communicable-disease, abuse, cyber or data, water, and animal risks.

Section II Coverage F is no-fault Medical Payments to Others coverage for qualifying third-party injury; the editions cover injury on an insured location and specified off-premises pathways, and 2023-02 expressly measures medical expenses within three years after the accident.

Attached HO 04 35 modifies loss-assessment treatment: its 2014-04 edition covers an insured's share of covered association property-loss or liability assessments up to $10,000, while its 2023-02 edition covers collective-property loss, a covered master-policy deductible, or covered association liability up to $25,000 and excludes ordinary maintenance, betterment, fines, business, contractual, and speculative assessments.

The HO-6 base form's loss-assessment additional coverage is $1,000 in 2014-04 and $2,000 in 2023-02, so those base limits must be distinguished from the higher HO 04 35 limit when that endorsement is attached.

HO 04 91 writes back unit-owner coverage for direct physical loss caused by sewer or drain backup and sump overflow or discharge to covered building and personal property, while preserving exclusions for flood, surface water, groundwater, gradual leakage, and repair of the failed system; it supplies a $7,500 limit and a $750 deductible.

Attached HO 17 32 is the repository's 2014-04 unit-owner rental endorsement: it applies while a unit is rented or held available, covers specified landlord-owned tenant-use property and loss of rent after a covered loss makes the unit unfit, excludes a tenant's personal property merely because it is present, and limits landlord's furnishings to $5,000.

HO-6 2023-02 separately provides $3,000 landlord's-furnishings coverage and fair-rental-value Coverage D language, so the 2014-04 HO 17 32 terms must not be applied to a 2023-02 policy without checking the policy schedule and attached endorsements.

Attached HO 17 33 modifies 2014-04 Coverage A by using a risk-of-direct-physical-loss grant for unit building property and setting a $25,000 Coverage A limit, while preserving its stated exclusions for flood, surface water, groundwater, sewer or sump backup, and other excluded causes.

The 2023-02 HO-6 source contains apparent drafting defects, including repeated wording in the vacancy definition and repeated words in endorsement cross-references, so those phrases should be flagged rather than silently normalized.

The 2024-03 HO-3 Section II Coverage E pays damages for which an insured is legally liable because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for covered claims or suits; Coverage E applies to insured locations and personal activities, applies separately to each insured, and does not increase the applicable limit through that separation.

HO-3 Section II Coverage F provides no-fault medical-payments coverage for necessary medical expenses from accidental bodily injury, including specified injuries away from an insured location, while its business exclusion preserves only activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits and its animal-away-from-location grant excludes animals used in connection with a business.

The HO-3 baseline Section II exclusions remove bodily injury and property damage arising from a business or business pursuit and separately constrain business-use vehicles, watercraft, and animals, subject to the stated incidental-to-nonbusiness exception.

HO 04 42 provides attached-endorsement coverage for an insured's bodily injury, property damage, or personal injury liability arising from an occurrence connected with a lawful incidental occupancy at premises used with the residence, where the occupancy is subordinate to residential use and does not materially change the premises' residential character; it provides a defense until the applicable limit is paid or coverage does not apply.

HO 04 42 uses the policy's insured status rather than expanding who is insured, and it excludes incidental occupancy away from the residence and numerous professional, care, product, employment, vehicle, equipment, pollution, disease, intentional-act, and criminal-act exposures; it also excludes unpermitted or non-residentially subordinate business activity.

HO 04 42 refers its liability grant to the applicable limit but does not state a separate dollar liability amount in the cited grant, while its later limit provisions are written for covered property; its claim duties include prompt notice, forwarding legal papers, cooperation, inspection, evidence preservation, and consent before voluntary payment or settlement.

HO 24 71 modifies the policy to provide personal-liability coverage for bodily injury or property damage and medical-payments coverage arising from an insured's business pursuit, defined as a continuous, regular, or profit-motivated business activity conducted from the residence or elsewhere; it covers specified premises, insured acts, and legally responsible persons without making another person an insured.

HO 24 71 sets a $100,000 maximum for the sum of all liability damages arising out of business pursuits, shared across insureds, claimants, claims, suits, and occurrences; payments reduce the amount available, defense costs do not reduce it, and the defense duty ends when payment exhausts the limit, while the endorsement does not increase the policy's personal-liability or medical-payments limits.

HO 24 73 modifies the policy for covered farming and farm premises, includes resident related household members and persons or organizations acting within the scope of duties performed for the insured in connection with covered farming, and grants bodily-injury/property-damage personal liability plus medical-payments coverage arising from covered personal activities, farming, or farm premises.

HO 24 73 applies the applicable personal-liability and medical-payments limits without stating a separate farm dollar limit in its cited grant, shares the limit across insureds and claimants, ends the defense after exhaustion, and retains business, professional-services, employee, workers-compensation, and business-animal exclusions.

HO 24 73 imposes farming-specific duties to maintain structures and animal controls, use care with agricultural materials and machinery, preserve operational records, report farm-operation claims, and notify the insurer of material changes, expansion, discontinuance, or transfer of control of the farming operation.

HO 24 82 modifies the policy by providing separate Personal Injury Coverage for an insured who is legally responsible for damages arising from covered offenses during the policy period, including false arrest, detention or imprisonment, malicious prosecution, wrongful eviction or entry, invasion of private occupancy, defamation, and privacy violations; the offense must arise from covered residence use or personal activities.

HO 24 82 excludes personal injury arising from business pursuits and business activities conducted from an insured location, except for activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits; its Personal Injury Limit of Liability is shared for all damages from an occurrence, is reduced by payments, does not increase through multiple insureds or claims, and ends the defense after judgments or settlements exhaust it.

HO 04 96 is titled as a no-Section-II liability-coverages endorsement, but its supplied operative text expressly grants personal liability, medical-payments, and defense coverage and supplies a general limit section without an operative Section II deletion clause; the source therefore requires reconciliation of the attached form, declarations, and controlling policy text before determining Section II availability.

Texas underwriting controls separately direct referral or non-acceptance for material business operations, agricultural activity, livestock, and certain animal exposures, and for premises used for business operations, professional services, production, farming, animal keeping, crop activity, or agricultural equipment; these are internal appetite controls rather than contractual coverage grants or exclusions.

The supplied DP-3 editions (2012-11, 2020-08, and 2026-01) are property-loss forms and do not contain Section II Coverage E—Personal Liability or Coverage F—Medical Payments to Others; their opening provisions instead insure direct physical loss to covered property.
The supplied HO-3, HO-4, HO-5, and HO-6 editions contain Section II Coverage E—Personal Liability and Coverage F—Medical Payments to Others as separate coverage sections.

Coverage E generally pays damages for which an insured is legally liable because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for a covered claim or suit, with the defense ending when the applicable liability limit is exhausted; the precise trigger and defense-cost wording varies by edition.

Coverage F generally pays necessary and reasonable medical expenses for accidental bodily injury to a qualifying person without regard to the insured's legal liability, subject to edition-specific timing, person, location/activity, exclusion, and limit wording.

The homeowners editions materially change liability and medical-payment claim decisions through different occurrence, coverage-territory, insured-location, animal, residence-employee, business, vehicle, watercraft, premises, electronic-data, communicable-disease, and other exclusion wording; a handler must use the actual edition rather than a generic remembered exclusion.

Section II additional coverages can pay defense-related expenses, emergency or first-aid expenses, damage to property of others, and loss assessments, but their wording and property-damage sublimits vary by edition and do not create Coverage E or F where the base form lacks those coverages.

Liability claim handling across the supplied editions depends on prompt notice and forwarding of legal papers, cooperation, records or examinations, consent before voluntary payments or settlements, preservation of evidence and recovery rights, and edition-specific legal-action, other-insurance, fraud, and misrepresentation conditions.

HO 04 96 is titled No Section II—Liability Coverages, but its operative W.1 provisions expressly provide personal liability coverage and medical payments coverage; the endorsement's operative wording must therefore be reconciled with the attached policy rather than treating the title alone as a removal of Coverage E/F.

HO 24 71 extends personal liability and medical-payments coverage to described business pursuits, preserves stated exclusions, and supplies a $100,000 business-pursuit limit that is not increased by the number of insureds, claimants, claims, suits, or occurrences.

HO 24 73 expands the described liability and medical-payments protection to covered farming and farm-premises risks, defines farming and farm premises, and retains exclusions and collective-limit rules for business, professional services, employee injury, property in care, vehicles, pollutants, abuse, and other listed exposures.

HO 24 82 adds personal-injury coverage for offenses including false arrest, malicious prosecution, wrongful eviction or entry, invasion of private occupancy, defamation, and privacy violations, provides a defense for covered claims or suits, and does not increase the applicable liability limit.

Coverage A is line-specific: DP-3 2012-11 and 2026-01 require 80% of dwelling replacement cost for replacement-cost settlement, DP-3 2020-08 requires 90%, the cited HO-3 and HO-5 editions require 80%, HO-6 covers unit-owner building property rather than the entire condominium building, and HO-4 2013-07/2021-10 expressly provide no Coverage A building insurance.

Coverage B limits vary by edition: the cited DP-3 2012-11, DP-3 2020-08, and HO-3/HO-5 editions state 10% of Coverage A, DP-3 2026-01 states 15%, and HO 04 48 (2026-06) replaces the HO-3 2024-03 base 10% limit with 20%; the supplied HO-4 and HO-6 Coverage B sections do not state a Coverage A-based percentage.

The cited HO-3 and HO-5 editions state Coverage C at 50% of Coverage A, while the supplied DP-3 2012-11, 2020-08, and 2026-01 forms state a 0% Coverage C limit; the supplied HO-4 and HO-6 Coverage C sections provide applicable limits and special limits without stating a Coverage C percentage in the cited sections.

Coverage D limits and architecture differ materially: the cited HO-3/HO-5 editions use 20% of Coverage A, HO-6 uses 50%, HO-4 2013-07 states 30% and HO-4 2021-10 states 40% despite their no-Coverage-A provisions, and DP-3 changes from a 20% FRV limit in 2012-11 to a 25% FRV limit in 2020-08 and a 30% aggregate Coverage D limit in 2026-01.

Coverage D responds to loss of use caused by a covered physical loss that makes the residence or rented part unfit, pays necessary increased living expense or actual lost fair rental value reduced by noncontinuing expenses, generally requires mitigation and records, and generally ends when the property is fit or access is restored.

HO 04 20 (2016-08) acts on the HO-3 Coverage A limit by adding 25% after the base limit is exhausted, while preserving the base Coverage A property grant, valuation method, exclusions, limitations, personal-property limit, and loss-of-use limit.

HO 04 40 (2011-05) writes back to the HO-3 2011 Coverage B rental exclusion by covering a qualifying rental structure on the residence premises and landlord furnishings up to $5,000, while expressly not providing personal-property, liability, or loss-of-use coverage for the rental structure.

HO 04 48 (2026-06) replaces the HO-3 2024-03 base Coverage B limit of 10% of Coverage A with 20% of Coverage A, but preserves the other Coverage B property, exclusion, duty, and deductible rules unless the endorsement conflicts with them.

HO 17 33 (2014-04) changes the HO-6 2014-04 Coverage A grant to coverage for a risk of direct physical loss subject to the endorsement's exclusions and limitations and sets a $25,000 Coverage A limit, instead of the base form's stated $5,000 default limit.

Coverage C special limits are generally inside the parent Coverage C limit rather than additional insurance; examples include HO-3 2018 special limits and HO-5 2022 special limits for money, jewelry, firearms, watercraft, silverware, business property, and vehicle-installed electronics.

The base-form peril structure differs between HO-3 and HO-5: the cited HO-3 2018 Coverage C enumerates named perils, while HO-5 2022 grants direct physical loss unless excluded and then states exclusions and ensuing-loss rules.

HO-6 Coverage A is unit-owner property and includes improvements, fixtures, appliances, and certain common property only to the extent of the owner's interest or legal responsibility; it is not automatically coverage for the condominium association's entire building.
The HO-3 2024-03 base form excludes loss caused by earth movement, including earthquake, while HO 04 54 supplies the earthquake-specific contract grant only when the endorsement is attached.

HO 04 54 edition 2009-04 is effective 2009-04-01 and is superseded by edition 2021-12 for policies effective on or after 2021-12-01, while remaining in force for policies written under the earlier edition.
HO 04 54 edition 2021-12 is effective 2021-12-01, applies only to loss involving an Earthquake while attached, and governs the policy package to which that edition is attached.

The 2009-04 endorsement covers direct physical loss to covered property caused by earthquake, including defined shaking, tremors, land shock waves, related earth shocks, buildings, structures, personal property, fixtures, foundations, falling, collapse, debris removal, and reasonable emergency measures.

The 2021-12 endorsement covers sudden and accidental direct physical loss to covered property caused by natural or artificial earthquake forces, including related aftershocks and earthquake-caused subsidence, settlement, sinking, rising, shifting, cracking, displacement, collapse, enumerated property, and specified ensuing losses.

Both HO 04 54 editions apply an aggregate earthquake limit across insureds, claims, property, and locations, reduce the remaining limit by payments, and include covered expenses such as emergency measures and debris removal within that limit; the form text does not state a numeric dollar amount.

The 2009-04 earthquake deductible is 5% of the applicable dwelling limit, or the highest applicable limit when no dwelling limit applies, with one deductible for an occurrence and separate deductibles for separate occurrences.

The 2021-12 earthquake deductible is 10% of the Coverage A limit and applies to the total covered earthquake loss across real and personal property, locations, and property coverages, without combining it with another deductible.

The 2009-04 edition excludes earth movement other than its covered earthquake loss, settling and structural movement, land value, ordinary maintenance, preexisting conditions, specified water causes, and post-earthquake deterioration, theft, vandalism, neglect, and loss-of-use categories.

The 2021-12 edition's exclusions preserve the distinction between earthquake-caused movement and other earth movement and exclude specified water events, land subsidence and slides, volcanic and wave events, defects, ordinary settlement, land and remediation costs, utility failures, progressive or preexisting damage, and unsupported consequential loss.

The 2009-04 conditions require notice within 90 days after discovery and require protection, preservation, inspection, cooperation, proof of loss, documentation, disclosure of other interests and insurance, and preservation of recovery rights.

The 2021-12 conditions require notice and reporting within 90 days after the loss occurs, protection and preservation of property, inspection access, cooperation, sworn proof and supporting records, and preservation of evidence and recovery rights; denial for noncompliance is limited by applicable law and material prejudice.

California HO 01 04 2021-06 applies to California property and interests, controls conflicting provisions under California law, states a 15% earthquake deductible based on applicable covered property value, groups the same earthquake occurrence, and requires 100% insured-to-value for replacement-cost settlement of a covered building.

California Bulletin CDI-2014-06 required an admitted insurer offering residential property insurance to make a clear earthquake offer, disclose material terms and a 10% seismic deductible, provide acceptance and declination processes, and preserve offer records; the bulletin is marked superseded by CDI-2022-03 for policies effective on or after 2022-03-14.

California Bulletin CDI-2022-03 requires an earthquake offer when issuing or renewing eligible residential property insurance, requires clear written or consented electronic disclosure of material terms including a 15% seismic deductible, prohibits inferred acceptance from silence, requires response records, and assigns responsibility for producer and third-party activity to the insurer.

California's mandatory offer and disclosure process is separate from the earthquake contract grant: the offer must identify that underlying residential property insurance may not cover earthquake, while earthquake coverage is issued only after required acceptance and documentation under the applicable policy and endorsement terms.

Base forms exclude fungi-related loss in edition-specific ways, and a microbial remediation limit or similar amount does not itself create coverage: HO-3 2024-03 excludes fungi, wet rot, dry rot, and bacteria while stating the microbial remediation limit does not create coverage for excluded loss; HO-4 2021-10 excludes those conditions whether visible or concealed; HO-5 2022-06 separately addresses fungi, fungi remediation costs, and bacteria or other microorganisms; HO-6 2023-02 excludes fungi, wet rot, dry rot, and bacteria except as provided by a limited fungi endorsement; and DP-3 2026-01 excludes presence, growth, spread, or removal of those conditions regardless of the contributing moisture source.

The HO 04 81 2018-09 endorsement is a narrow modification of the base policy rather than blanket fungi coverage: the base HO-3 exclusion remains the starting point, while the endorsement says it modifies the policy, leaves other terms and exclusions in force unless changed, and provides no coverage beyond its express terms.

HO 04 81 covers fungi-related direct physical loss only when a covered cause first causes direct physical loss to covered property and the fungi-related loss results from that physical loss; fungi loss that does not result from a covered cause is not covered.

When the HO 04 81 coverage trigger is satisfied, its expressly covered costs can include direct physical loss to covered property, reasonable and necessary removal, tear-out and replacement needed to access or repair covered property, post-remediation air or property testing when there is reason to believe fungi remain, and reasonable and necessary remediation related to covered direct physical loss.

Under HO 04 81, remediation is defined broadly as measures to remove, contain, treat, clean, dispose of, or otherwise address fungi, but it is covered only when reasonable and necessary for fungi for which coverage is provided and when related to covered direct physical loss.

HO 04 81 excludes fungi loss arising from constant or repeated seepage or leakage, constant or repeated discharge or overflow, flood, preexisting conditions, deterioration, decay, wear, neglect, inadequate maintenance, and defective work; it also preserves other policy exclusions unless the endorsement expressly changes them.

HO 04 81 does not cover monitoring without covered direct physical loss, preventive maintenance, routine cleaning, periodic inspection, non-covered investigation or remediation expenses, replacement of undamaged property solely because fungi are present or suspected, upgrades or redesign, work on non-covered property, or costs otherwise excluded or not expressly covered.

For HO 04 81 edition 2018-09, the fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria aggregate limit is $10,000 for all covered loss during the policy term, applies to covered property and related covered costs across locations, claims, insureds, property types, causes, and occurrences, and is reduced by payments without restoration; costs above the aggregate are not covered.
HO 04 81 applies the applicable policy deductible to covered fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria loss, and compliance with the endorsement's duties does not increase the available coverage.

For an HO 04 81 claim, the insured must report the loss within 30 days under the endorsement's conditions, identify the affected property and known circumstances, protect property, preserve damaged property and evidence when reasonably possible, permit inspection and testing, cooperate, and provide relevant records and claim-supporting documents.

HO 04 27 Limited Water Damage Coverage 2016-05 is not a general fungi write-back: it covers specified water discharges and system or appliance events, expressly excludes loss caused by fungi, wet rot, dry rot, or bacteria, and separately states a $5,000 fungi-related amount that must be read with that exclusion rather than treated alone as a coverage grant.

The North Carolina HO 01 32 amendatory endorsement 2018-05 states a $5,000 maximum for all loss caused by fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria regardless of the number of insureds, claims, damaged properties, or occurrences, states that such loss is not covered unless expressly provided, and defines fungi and wet rot in its definitions section.

North Carolina's NCDOI-2018-03 bulletin imposes disclosure and administrative requirements separate from contract coverage: when an applicable fungi limitation exists, an admitted property insurer must provide a clear, prominent, understandable, policy-consistent disclosure, make it available for new coverage before acceptance, update it for material renewal or policy changes, maintain delivery and control records, and remain responsible for agent or producer delivery.

For North Carolina claims involving alleged fungi loss, the bulletin requires fact review and reasonable investigation rather than an automatic denial, evaluation of whether a covered cause produced the condition, distinction between fungi damage and other covered damage, a clear written explanation for a limitation or partial denial, and preservation of the claim-file basis for the decision.

Water-backup analysis must distinguish reverse flow through a sewer or drain from discharge or overflow of a sump system, identify the already-insured property and insured interest, then read the base exclusion together with the attached edition-specific endorsement; water near a drain or sump is not by itself proof of backup.

HO 04 90 (2010-10), effective 2010-10-01, writes back accidental direct physical loss to covered property caused by sewer/drain backup or sump discharge/overflow and reasonable emergency measures, subject to a $5,000 aggregate limit and a $500 endorsement deductible; the edition is superseded for policies effective on or after 2027-01-01 but remains in force for policies written under it.

HO 04 90 (2027-01), effective 2027-01-01, writes back Water Backup and Sump Discharge or Overflow for direct physical loss and reasonable protective measures, expressly permits sudden or gradual occurrence subject to its exclusions, and modifies the HO-3 base exclusion to the extent stated; its aggregate limit is $10,000 and its deductible is $1,000 per covered occurrence.

HO 04 91 (2019-03), effective 2019-03-01, writes back sewer/drain backup and sump overflow/discharge for an HO-6 unit-owner's covered building property, improvements and betterments, fixtures, appliances, floor coverings, interior finishes, and covered personal property, plus stated water-removal, cleaning, drying, and debris expenses; its aggregate limit is $7,500 and deductible is $750.

HO 04 92 (2019-03), effective 2019-03-01, writes back sewer/drain backup and sump discharge/overflow only for a tenant's covered personal property; it does not insure the landlord's building, and it provides a $2,500 aggregate limit with a $250 deductible.

DP 04 95 (2021-05), effective 2021-05-01, writes back direct physical loss to property already covered by the DP policy from sewer/drain backup or sump, pump, or related-equipment overflow/discharge and covers necessary reasonable emergency measures; its aggregate limit is $5,000 and its deductible is $1,000.

DP-3 2026-01 contains an edition-specific internal control point: E.67 states sudden-and-accidental water-backup coverage while X.6 says backup and sump overflow are excluded unless DP 04 95 is attached and X.7 refers to a backup-and-sump-overflow limit; E.67 supplies no standalone amount, so the declarations and attached DP 04 95 must be verified before applying coverage or a limit.

The recurring endorsement boundary is resulting direct physical loss to otherwise covered property rather than repair, replacement, clearing, or improvement of the failed sewer, drain, sump, pump, valve, or related equipment; flood, surface water, below-ground water, repeated seepage or leakage, maintenance or defective-condition losses, and avoidable additional damage remain subject to edition-specific exclusions.

The endorsement-specific reporting deadlines in the cited editions are 30 days for HO 04 90 (2010-10), 30 days after discovery for HO 04 90 (2027-01), 60 days after discovery for HO 04 91, 90 days after discovery for HO 04 92, and 30 days for DP 04 95; the duties also require mitigation, preservation, inspection access, records, cooperation, and preservation of recovery rights.

HO 04 91 adds unit-owner controls for common systems, including cooperation with a property manager or condominium association, access to common plumbing or drainage areas, reporting common-system defects, and retaining related maintenance and repair records.

HO 04 92's grant is limited to tenant personal property and does not itself add a loss-of-use grant; any additional living expense or fair-rental-value issue must be tested against the base HO-4 Coverage D terms and the policy's covered-loss requirements.

Illinois Bulletin IDOI-2017-10 is a state-overlay disclosure and claims-handling requirement, not a substitute for contract terms: it requires clear, conspicuous, retainable disclosure of availability, sewer/drain/sump scope, limits, deductibles, exclusions, and conditions in connection with sale, issuance, renewal, or material endorsement change, plus records and consistency across policy communications.

The Illinois bulletin states that the disclosure must identify the most the insurer will pay and states $5,000 in B.2.6, but that overlay figure does not replace the cited endorsements' contract limits of $2,500, $5,000, $7,500, or $10,000; apparent differences must be resolved by the filed policy and attached endorsement.

For Illinois water-backup claims, the bulletin requires reasonable investigation, evaluation of the actual policy and endorsements, a written explanation identifying the relied-on provision and its application to known facts when coverage is denied or limited, and payment of an undisputed covered portion unless barred by policy or law; it does not create coverage that the contract excludes.

Coverage must be analyzed by the policy's line, edition, coverage part, water source and route, and attached endorsements; the supplied DP-3, HO-3, HO-4, HO-5, and HO-6 editions define materially different property parts and loss-of-use grants.

For the supplied current editions, accidental plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, sprinkler, or appliance discharge can cover direct physical loss under the applicable line-specific water grant, while the system or appliance from which the water escaped is generally excluded; DP-3 2026-01 also contains an Additional Coverages E discharge provision with reasonable access.

Continuous, repeated, gradual or over-time seepage, leakage, overflow, and discharge are excluded under the supplied DP-3 2026-01, HO-3 2024-03, HO-4 2021-10, HO-5 2022-06, and HO-6 2023-02 wording, with separate exclusions for source repair, deterioration, and leakage through building openings.

Freezing coverage is conditioned on protective action that varies by edition but generally requires reasonable care to maintain heat or shut off water and drain the system, with vacancy or unoccupancy exclusions in the cited DP-3, HO-3, HO-4, HO-5, and HO-6 editions.

The current base forms exclude flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, body-of-water overflow or spray, and water below the surface of the ground; DP-3 2026-01 expressly applies its flood exclusion whether the water is driven by wind or otherwise.

HO-3 2024-03 excludes loss caused directly or indirectly by excluded perils regardless of concurrent or sequential contributing causes, and separately excludes waterborne material moved by excluded water and water entering through an opening created by excluded water.

Rain, snow, sleet, sand or dust entering through a roof or wall is covered only when the applicable form's covered wind, hail, or other covered peril first damages the building and creates an opening; HO 04 27 preserves that opening boundary.

DP 04 95 Water Backup — Dwelling Property (2021-05), when attached, writes back the DP sewer, drain and sump boundary only for direct physical loss from sudden water or waterborne-material backup or sump overflow, while preserving exclusions for openings, flood, surface water, below-ground water, maintenance failure, repeated seepage, fungi, and failed-equipment repair.

DP 04 95 Water Backup — Dwelling Property (2021-05) has a $5,000 Water Backup limit and a $1,000 deductible applied once to the same covered water-backup loss, and those amounts do not create coverage for otherwise excluded damage.

Coverage D or E loss-of-use benefits are derivative: the cited HO-3, HO-4, HO-5, HO-6 and DP-3 editions require a covered direct physical loss or covered loss to make the residence or rental part uninhabitable or unfit, so an excluded water event does not independently create loss-of-use coverage.

The base fungi exclusions in the cited DP-3, HO-3, HO-4, HO-5 and HO-6 editions remove fungi, wet rot, dry rot, bacteria or microorganisms, with the HO forms' exact write-back references varying by edition.

HO 04 81 Limited Fungi, Wet or Dry Rot, or Bacteria Coverage (2018-09), when attached, writes back the applicable HO base fungi exclusion only when a covered cause first causes direct physical loss to covered property and the fungi loss results from that loss; it preserves exclusions for repeated seepage or discharge, flood, preexisting conditions, neglect, maintenance and defective work.

HO 04 81 can cover necessary fungi removal, access tear-out, repair-related tear-out, remediation and limited post-remediation testing after covered direct physical loss, but excludes preventive monitoring, routine cleaning, undamaged-property replacement, upgrades and otherwise excluded water damage; its fungi aggregate is $10,000 for all covered loss during the policy term and covered payments reduce the remaining amount.

HO 04 27 Limited Water Damage Coverage (2016-05) grants specified accidental discharge or overflow and certain source-system breakage, cracking, bulging or freezing, but preserves exclusions for constant or repeated seepage, backup, below-ground water, flood, surface water and maintenance-related sources; its separate $5,000 fungi figure does not override its express fungi exclusion.

A windstorm or hail deductible applies only to covered direct physical loss to covered property; it does not create coverage or override an exclusion. The current HO-3 covers direct physical loss caused by windstorm and hail subject to exclusions and conditions, and HO 23 77 2022-07 expressly preserves otherwise uncovered property, loss, and damage.

Under the current HO-3 opening rule, wind-driven rain, snow, sleet, sand, or dust entering a building is covered only when the direct force of wind or hail first damages the building and creates an opening; the deductible does not itself make water damage covered.

For a percentage deductible, the selected percentage is applied to the applicable limit for the damaged covered property rather than ordinarily to the repair estimate; covered-loss valuation and applicable policy terms are determined before the deductible is subtracted, and separate applicable limits are not combined solely to reduce it.

Occurrence or loss-event language controls aggregation: related windstorm or hail damage from the same weather event is generally treated as one occurrence or loss event, while separate weather events may receive separate deductibles; later discovery alone does not create a new event.

A windstorm or hail deductible generally remains separate from a deductible for another peril, but the controlling form determines whether another deductible applies to a separate cause and prevents duplicate deductions for the same covered loss unless its terms clearly require otherwise.

Covered emergency measures, temporary or protective repairs, debris removal, and covered loss-of-use or related expenses remain subject to the applicable windstorm or hail deductible when the policy covers them; the deductible does not independently create coverage for those expenses.

HO 23 77 2014-02 permits a selected windstorm or hail percentage from 1% through 5%, while HO 23 77 2022-07 permits 2% through 10%; the 2014-02 edition remains applicable to policies written under it after the later edition superseded it.

Florida DP 01 09 2021-03 sets a 2% to 10% windstorm and hail deductible and requires at least 45 days' notice before an increase, while Florida HO 01 09 2023-07 sets a 2% to 15% deductible and requires at least 60 days' written notice before an increase.

Florida OIR-2022-01 is a disclosure overlay that requires the hurricane or named-storm deductible disclosure to identify the trigger, distinguish other deductibles, describe the calculation basis, and state a named-storm minimum of 2% and hurricane maximum of 10%; it expressly does not establish a minimum Section I deductible.

Colorado DOI-2013-01 is superseded by DOI-2019-05 for policies effective on or after May 20, 2019; the earlier bulletin capped a windstorm or hail deductible at 3% of the applicable property coverage limit, while DOI-2019-05 caps it at 5% of applicable covered loss and requires 30 days' written notice before an increase.

Colorado HO 01 05 2022-10 implements DOI-2019-05 in the contract by setting a 1% to 5% windstorm and hail deductible range and applying it only to covered direct physical loss, including when windstorm or hail acts with another cause.

Texas B-2021-08 requires a named-storm windstorm and hail deductible of at least 1%, caps a hurricane deductible at 5%, caps a seacoast-territory windstorm deductible at 10%, requires claim support for the deductible, and requires 30 days' notice before an increase plus a 72-hour continuation after a named-storm designation ends when the policy uses such a period.

Texas contract editions differ: HO 01 45 2022-01 uses a 1% to 5% windstorm or hail deductible and 45 days' notice before an increase, while DP 01 45 2022-01 uses a 1% to 10% deductible and 30 days' notice.

Louisiana LDI-2012-05 is superseded by LDI-2020-07 for policies effective on or after July 15, 2020; the 2020 bulletin caps a hurricane deductible at 5% of applicable covered loss, requires 30 days' advance written notice before an increase in a windstorm deductible, and requires a named-storm period to continue 72 hours after the designation ends.

Louisiana HO 01 17 2020-09 applies a 2% to 5% windstorm and hail deductible to covered direct physical loss, treats related damage from the same event as one occurrence, requires 30 days' notice before an increase, and defines a named-storm period that continues 72 hours after the designation ends.

HO-3 2024-03 Coverage B covers qualifying detached or similarly separated other structures on the residence premises, uses a 10% of Coverage A additional-insurance limit, and excludes business, farming, dwelling, land, and outdoor-property uses stated in the base form.

HO-6 2023-02 Coverage B requires an other structure to be separately set apart and solely owned by an insured; it excludes rented structures except a private garage, most business use, and association- or third-party-owned structures, and its supplied Coverage B text states no percentage limit.

HO 04 48 (2026-06) modifies HO-3 Coverage B by replacing the applicable limit with 20% of Coverage A, while keeping the Coverage B limit collective for an occurrence and subject to the existing property qualifications, exclusions, conditions, and deductible.

HO 04 40 (2011-05) writes back property coverage for a qualifying structure rented or held for rental on the residence premises, covering the insured's interest and specified attached property, but leaves non-premises property, tenant property, liability, loss of use, business pursuits, and listed causes of loss excluded.
HO 04 40 applies a $5,000 collective limit to landlord's furnishings and requires evidence that the structure was rented or held available for rental at the time of loss.

HO 04 10 (2011-05) recognizes a lawful financial interest in covered property without making the holder an insured, transferring ownership, or granting rights beyond the described interest; the interest must be established and remain valid at the time of loss.

Under HO 04 10, an additional interest has no separate limit unless expressly provided, cannot enlarge the covered property or causes of loss, and shares the applicable limit with the policyholder through joint or direct payment.

HO 04 41 (2011-05) extends only liability insured status for covered bodily injury or property damage arising from ownership, maintenance, or use of the endorsed residence premises; it does not provide property insurance for the additional insured.

HO 04 41 keeps the additional insured's liability within the applicable shared occurrence limit and does not increase that limit for additional insureds, claimants, allegations, or legal theories; the additional insured must provide notice, suit papers, cooperation, and change information.

HO 04 42 (2011-05) provides coverage for a scheduled incidental occupancy conducted by an insured at premises used with the residence only when the occupancy is subordinate to residential use, lawful, and not materially disruptive of the premises' residential character.

HO 04 42 excludes unpermitted or materially different occupancies, unrelated businesses, and numerous specialized exposures, does not increase the other-structures, contents, ALE, or debris-removal percentages, and requires scheduled activity, licensing, change notice, records, and inspection compliance.

HO 17 32 (2014-04) changes HO-6 treatment while a unit is rented or held available for rental, covering qualifying owner-owned rental-unit property and loss of rent after covered damage while excluding a tenant's personal property merely because it is in the unit; landlord's furnishings are limited to $5,000.

HO-6 2023-02 places unit-owner building property under Coverage A when the owner has the required ownership or repair responsibility, while HO 17 33 (2014-04) separately modifies Coverage A to a risk-of-direct-physical-loss grant with a $25,000 limit and preserves its stated water and earth-movement exclusions.

Attachment of a permitted-occupancy endorsement does not override internal underwriting eligibility: Texas guidance requires detached structures to be safe, maintained, and incidental to residential use, while underwriting guidance requires referral for business activity and approval before classifying activity as incidental, including detached structures used for business.

HO 04 35 is an attachment-dependent endorsement whose provisions control conflicting policy provisions while nonconflicting policy terms remain applicable; the supplied 2014-04 edition is superseded by 2023-02 for policies effective on or after 2023-02-01, while the older edition remains applicable to policies written under it, and both source files identify the endorsement line as HO-6.

HO 04 35 (2014-04) covers an insured's allocated assessment from an authorized association when it results from covered direct physical loss to association property or from a liability claim against the association, and it can cover an association deductible arising from a covered loss when the association's property insurance applies.

HO 04 35 (2023-02) covers an assessment legally charged to an owner or tenant for covered direct physical loss to Collective Property, an association Master Policy deductible tied to covered loss, or Property Damage for which the association is legally liable and that results from a covered occurrence.

The maximum Loss Assessment Coverage limit is $10,000 under HO 04 35 (2014-04) and $25,000 under HO 04 35 (2023-02); payments reduce available coverage and the limit is not increased by multiple insureds, claims, assessments, or associations.

Neither HO 04 35 edition states a numeric deductible: 2014-04 applies the applicable policy deductible to a covered assessment and once to the same covered loss or liability claim, while 2023-02 applies the applicable deductible only to the covered assessment amount before payment and does not apply it to uncovered charges.

Both editions require a valid, enforceable, properly allocated assessment and prompt notice with supporting records; the 2023-02 edition additionally requires notice of changes such as revision, withdrawal, reduction, increase, or reallocation.

HO 04 35 payment is limited to the insured's covered allocated share and is reduced by duplicate or legally available recovery; both editions preserve duties to cooperate, protect property, preserve evidence, and avoid unauthorized voluntary payments or settlements.

The editions exclude assessment charges for ordinary maintenance or improvement, wear or deterioration, defective design or workmanship, intentional or criminal conduct, fines or penalties, contractual-only obligations, and excluded causes of loss; they also preserve applicable policy exclusions unless the endorsement expressly provides otherwise.

HO-6 2014-04 base additional coverage provides a $1,000 property loss-assessment grant but excludes assessments imposed because of an insured's liability or breach of contract; attaching HO 04 35 (2014-04) modifies that base assessment treatment and its limit through the endorsement's controlling provisions.

HO-6 2023-02 base additional coverage provides a $2,000 assessment grant and does not reduce Coverage C; attaching HO 04 35 (2023-02) modifies the base assessment scope and limit through the endorsement's $25,000 Collective Property, master-policy-deductible, and property-damage-liability provisions.

HO 04 35 assessment coverage is distinct from ordinary Coverage E personal liability: Coverage E pays an insured's legally owed damages and may defend a covered suit, whereas HO 04 35 pays an association assessment and does not create a duty to defend the association.

The customer FAQ instructs staff not to assume an association assessment is covered and to identify why it was issued and what property or loss it concerns before discussing payment.
